title: Caracas After Maduro: an improvised transition
oneLine: US forces seized Maduro in January 2026; his deputy now runs Venezuela with Washington's blessing, while a US oil blockade leaves Cuba in the dark.

whoIsWho.stance: Acting president; trades oil and cooperation for survival, promises elections with no date.
Nobel laureate and opposition leader; wants a real election, soon.
Captured a dictator; now wants oil deals, an election and no Marines on the ground.
Leads Cuba through blackouts and a US blockade; talks with Washington, gives little.
Aged 95, still the weight behind Cuba's old guard.

whyItMatters: Venezuela sits on the world's largest proven oil reserves and eight million of its people have fled. How the transition ends, by a vote, a deal or a coup, decides US influence in Latin America and whether Cuba's system survives.

timeline.text: Hugo Chávez dies; Nicolás Maduro succeeds him.
Maduro claims a disputed election that independent counts say he lost.
A US raid captures Maduro, who is flown to trial in New York.
Delcy Rodríguez is sworn in as acting president.
A US oil blockade of Cuba begins; blackouts spread.
The US embassy in Caracas reopens.
At the UN, Rodríguez promises elections but names no date.
